title: Key squares
line: Lead with the king: the squares that make the pawn promote.

steps.text: For a pawn on e4, the key squares are the three squares two rows ahead: d6, e6 and f6.
With your king on a key square, the pawn promotes whoever is to move. An edge pawn is the exception; a later lesson shows why.
Tap the three key squares of this pawn.
steps.hint: Two rows ahead of this pawn: the square in front and one to each side.
steps.after: Two rows ahead, in front and to each side.

steps.text: Lead with the king. Step onto a key square of this pawn.

wrong.e3e4: The pawn moved first, so its key squares moved up with it, and the black king guards them. The game is drawn.
wrong.f4e4: Black answers by facing your king, and no key square is in reach. The game is drawn.

steps.hint: Two of the ringed squares are one step away.
steps.after: Your king is on a key square. The pawn will promote, whatever Black does.

steps.text: Here no key square is in reach yet. Put your king in front of the pawn first.

wrong.d4d5: The pawn went first. The black king blocks it, and the game is drawn.
wrong.e4e5: Beside the pawn is not in front of it. Black keeps your king off the key squares, and the game is drawn.

steps.hint: Stand on the square straight in front of the pawn.
steps.after: Black has to give way, and your king reaches a key square next.

summary: The king leads, the pawn follows. A king on a key square makes the pawn promote, unless it is an edge pawn.
